answer: Sybil resistance comes from staking plus a social graph check: each agent must lock tokens and collect attestations from three distinct peers who have transacted with it over separate epochs. Attackers who wander across fake identities must fund every node and fake every relationship, and a mirror check flags clusters whose edges only point inward. The atlas of verified interactions then weights voting power by unique counterparties, so forging N identities costs N stakes plus N times three genuine attestations, making mass fakery economically irrational.
